svg.text: Claude Code owns the memory directory. hyprlayer finds it, shows it, lets you edit a file in it, and hands its index to codex tabs.
Hyprlayer.app — sends a workstream id and a bare file name
the lightbulb in the sidebar panel's header
fetched only while it is open
reads a file through the existing getDoc
a pencil on files the listing holds
hyprlayer-server — the runtime, on the machine the memory lives on
free functions over explicit paths — no runtime import
one arm each, straight to the facade
Claude Code's own — one per repository
the index — Claude loads the first
gets the index at thread start,
reads topic files, asked not to write
the save takes the same route, ending in save_project_memory_file
and it writes only inside the memory directory
its transcript, for the key check
The key is Claude Code's convention, not ours
The encoding, the autoMemoryDirectory precedence and the index bounds
are ported from Claude Code and were checked against 2.1.252, .258,
.270, .273 and .274. There is no version gate: if a release moves the
directory, the key check reports a mismatch and the view and codex both
The sandbox, not the preamble, stops a codex write
Under Default and Accept-edits the directory is outside codex's
writable roots, and Plan runs read-only. Bypass permissions runs
danger-full-access, where the preamble's request is the only thing
The one write path is contained
A bare *.md name, an existing regular file, no symlinked target, a
stale-write guard, and an O_EXCL temp file. The Library's own save
still renames through a fixed temp name (library.rs, gitops.rs); that
